page: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The configuration provides 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong multi-core profile alongside high memory throughput. While single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and gzip compression tests, multi-core execution is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations ranking in the top 25 percent. Additionally, the server demonstrates high efficiency in database operations, achieving strong results in Redis SET operations and Passmark encryption tests.

The primary tradeoff of the r5b.24xlarge is its reliance on external storage and its lack of GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for heavy graphics processing or large-scale LLM text generation. However, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong multi-threaded performance make it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is well-suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and high-throughput data processing tasks.
